# Every package is pinned to a version and to the hash of every file PyPI serves for it.
# One hash anywhere puts pip in hash checking mode, where it wants one for everything it
# installs, which is why the packages nobody here asked for by name are written down too.
#
# This covers the file pip downloads, and nothing a build then does on its own. Connectrum
# is the one built here rather than unpacked, and it needs no wheel, being pure Python.
# Coincurve is the one that would do work of its own: it compiles C and fetches libsecp256k1
# over the network wherever its wheels do not reach. They reach CPython 3.8 to 3.12 on
# macOS x86_64 and arm64, and on Linux x86_64, aarch64 and i686; on Windows they reach
# amd64 over that same range and arm64 from 3.9 on. Anything outside that, a newer Python
# among it, is where the build happens. That fetch is pinned to a commit of
# bitcoin-core/secp256k1 and checked against a sha256 by the build itself.
#
# To add a package, take its hashes from https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json
